title: Administrative discretion and legal and political accountability
shortTitle: Administrative discretion and legal and political accountability
summary: Administrative accountability consists of mechanisms that allow institutions and the public to identify, evaluate, and constrain official decisions.
notes:
Legal accountability may come from statutory standards, required reasons, administrative procedures, and judicial review. Political accountability may come from elections, appointment and removal, legislative oversight, and renewed authorization. Their effectiveness depends on timing, information, institutional capacity, and the distribution of responsibility.

Amalgamated Meat Cutters relies on temporary authorization and review but is followed by doubts about how an emergency program could actually be supervised. Gorsuch’s Gundy dissent worries that delegation lets Congress and the Executive exchange blame. Mashaw argues that discretion can make government responsive to presidential elections when new legislation is hard to enact. Arthrex emphasizes visible responsibility through superior review of agency adjudication, while its dissenters emphasize expertise and protection against political interference. These mechanisms involve different institutional tradeoffs.
